newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait issues permits for three steel mills.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait issues permits for three steel mills.

text.p: Kuwait has issued permits for private investors to build three steel mills with a combined annual capacity of 478,887 tonnes, the official Kuwait News Agency (KUNA) reported on Tuesday.
"The General Industry Authority announced today (Tuesday) that permits have been issued for the establishment of three mills to produce steel for the first time in Kuwait," KUNA said.
"The production from the three mills will cover the local market," it added. Kuwait's current annual consumption is estimated at around 400,000 tonnes.
"The construction of these mills will take from one to two years," an official told the agency, noting that construction work would start in 1997.
The largest of the three would produce 300,000 tonnes of steel bars per year using materials imported from Iran and other countries.
Another would produce 128,887 tonnes using material from Saudi Arabia and the third, with a 50,000 tonne steel bar capacity, will use scrap steel, the official added.
The mills would be owned by private investors mainly from Kuwait along with some investors from fellow Gulf states.
Iranian Economy and Finance Minister Morteza Mohammadkhan, who arrived in Kuwait on Monday, said he plans to discuss with Kuwaiti officials a proposed $70 million joint steel mill.

But he refused to say if the Gulf neighbours were close to finalising the deal between the National Iranian Steel Company (Nisco) and private Kuwaiti investors to set up the steel reinforced bar mill in Kuwait.
